requirement:
The `habeas author` workflow MUST support authoring and refreshing exception
evidence under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. Assessment
inputs MUST include the current file or function source, the built-in's fixed
text, and its citation commentary under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.

Justifications and their assessment evidence MUST be retainable in Git
independently of the disposable coverage artifacts under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage`. Raw profiles, coverage reports, and
captured source snapshots MUST NOT be required in Git to validate an exception
against freshly collected coverage.
rationale:
structural: I found no structural obligation in `requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions.author`, so no implementation root needs `{impl}` evidence. No review roots were supplied. I tested each clause by asking whether a different implementation could produce the same observable results and still break the clause.

- **"The `habeas author` workflow MUST support authoring and refreshing exception evidence"**: This is a workflow capability. It says nothing about which library, type, signature or delegation interface to use. Any internal design that lets the user author and refresh exception evidence satisfies it.
- **"Assessment inputs MUST include the current file or function source, the built-in's fixed text, and its citation commentary"**: This lists the content the assessor receives. Building the prompt from different helpers, or in a different order, gives the same inputs, so it is observable behavior. It does not prescribe a named interface. The input-assembly format is also set by the cited `requirements.references.citation_review` and its own refining declarations. Those declarations are judged separately.
- **"Justifications and their assessment evidence MUST be retainable in Git independently of the disposable coverage artifacts"**: This constrains where evidence lives. It must be outside `target/habeas/coverage/` and not tied to the SQLite store. It names no type, field or API. Any storage layout that keeps the evidence apart from the coverage artifacts has the same observable result.
- **"Raw profiles, coverage reports, and captured source snapshots MUST NOT be required in Git to validate an exception against freshly collected coverage"**: This is a validation behavior. Validation either needs those artifacts or it doesn't, and you can tell by running it. It prescribes no code structure.

The cited requirements `requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`, `requirements.references.citation_review` and `requirements.test-coverage.storage` give context only. Their own obligations are assessed against their own text. Every clause here is behavioral or about data placement, so this requirement needs no implementation-root evidence.

behavioral: ## Obligations and test mapping

**1. `habeas author` supports authoring and refreshing exception evidence, with assessment inputs of the current source, the built-in's fixed text and the citation commentary.**

The test is `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[coverage_explanations_use_standard_citation_authoring_and_freshness]`. It authors `citations:src/lib.rs#fn[helper]`, where the item cites `habeas:coverage` in fenced commentary. It asserts three things about the inputs:
- The mandatory inputs hold the item's current source text (`fn helper() {}`) and a 64-character hash.
- They hold the `habeas:coverage` built-in's fixed text, checked by the `difficulty alone` phrase.
- The initial prompt contains the commentary (`Defensive invariant abort`) and the built-in citation-review criteria.

It then runs `assess`. The record is accepted. It names `habeas:coverage` as a citation and has an input for `src/lib.rs` and `fn[helper]` with the matching hash. It stores the evidence at `evidence/citations/src/lib.rs/fn[helper].json`, reloads it, and checks that the reload matches.

For refreshing, the test edits the source, so the citation commentary changes. It asserts that `validate_review` reports `citations changed`, which makes the evidence stale and in need of refresh.

`src/execution_coverage/check.rs#mod[tests]/fn[standard_inline_doc_and_fenced_commentary_reviews_track_their_explanations]` also tracks freshness for both forms:
- It covers an inline doc comment explanation and fenced commentary.
- Reviews are accepted when current.
- They become non-accepted, with errors, when the doc text or the commentary changes.

The generic re-authoring mechanics (`--missing` and `--force`) belong to `requirements.authoring.refresh`. `requirements.references.citation_review` cites that requirement, so this requirement does not need to retest it.

**2. Justifications and assessment evidence are retainable in Git independently of the disposable coverage artifacts. Raw profiles, coverage reports and captured source snapshots must not be required in Git to validate an exception against freshly collected coverage.**

The `check.rs` test builds a fixture with only source and `evidence/citations/...` review files. No profiles, reports or snapshots exist. `exceptions()` still accepts the exception.

The test then copies only the review JSON into a second, separate checkout of the same source. It asserts the exception is accepted there with no errors. This shows that only Git-retainable evidence is needed and that identities are checkout-portable. Both are required by this text and by `requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`.

I did not reassess the cited `requirements.test-coverage.storage`, `requirements.references.citation_review` or `requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`.

No gap found.

text: :::{req} check.exceptions.author
The `habeas author` workflow MUST support authoring and refreshing exception
evidence under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. Assessment
inputs MUST include the current file or function source, the built-in's fixed
text, and its citation commentary under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
Justifications and their assessment evidence MUST be retainable in Git
independently of the disposable coverage artifacts under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage`. Raw profiles, coverage reports, and
captured source snapshots MUST NOT be required in Git to validate an exception
against freshly collected coverage.
:::{req} check.exceptions
An unmet file threshold or an unexecuted or not-measured function MAY satisfy
the coverage policy only
through current, accepted, independently assessed evidence explaining why its
coverage is incomplete. An exception MUST be attached to the source file or
function whose incomplete coverage it justifies. A file-threshold exception
MUST NOT automatically excuse untested functions.
An exception MUST NOT excuse another source item's incomplete coverage.
Changes to the source item, justification, or other inputs
of its citation review MUST invalidate the affected exception under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
A source comment or unassessed justification alone MUST NOT count as accepted
exception evidence. Function and gap identities MUST remain portable between
equivalent local and CI checkouts rather than depend on checkout paths,
run identifiers, timestamps, or process identifiers.
:::{req} citation_review
Every source item outside the book that carries at least one `{cite}` reference
other than a citation of `habeas:util` under {cite}`requirements.references.util`
MUST have a citation review: an assessment of that item's citations, recorded at
`evidence/citations/<file>/<selector>.json`, where `<file>` is the item's
project-relative path, `<selector>` is its outline selector with every `/` and
`%` percent-encoded, and the root node uses `_root`. The review MUST use the
prompt defined by {cite}`requirements.authoring.citation_prompt`. For citations
of project requirements and examples, the reviewer MUST assess whether the item
should be re-checked or kept in sync when the cited definition changes, and
whether the reference procedure of
{cite}`requirements.references.procedure` calls for `{impl}` or `{test}` instead.
For citations of built-ins, the reviewer MUST check the permitted reference
roles and forms and any citation-review criteria stated in the built-in's fixed
text, using the item's source and commentary. A permitted citation role alone
MUST NOT suffice when the fixed text states additional criteria. Mandatory inputs,
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, MUST be the item's outline
node, each cited declaration or built-in text, and the citations' commentary. The record MUST contain the item's file and selector,
its citations by role, name, and commentary, `determination`, `rationale`, and
`inputs`, with determinations under {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`. Validation
MUST require a current, accepted review for every such item and report stale,
missing, or orphaned reviews; a review MUST become stale when the item's hash,
a cited declaration, or its citations or their commentary change. Authoring with
`--all` MUST include citation reviews, and `habeas author citations:<file>#<selector>`
MUST author the review of the one item it names, under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`, where omitting `#<selector>`
names the file's root node. A citation in a requirement or example
declaration is reviewed as part of that definition's own assessment instead.
Fenced commentary elsewhere in the book is reviewed under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review.book_commentary`.
Storage MAY use the versioned representation under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.habeas.evidence_format`, retaining the same review
information and validation rules.
:::{req} storage
Execution coverage is stored as disposable build artifacts under
`habeas/coverage/` in the project's Cargo target directory
(`target/habeas/coverage/` with default Cargo settings). A SQLite database is
the primary store for current test results, processed measurements, and the
metadata identifying their collection invocation. Raw LLVM profiles and
captured source may remain separate files referenced by those results.
The invocation metadata identifies the invocation, capture time, command,
selected tests, and, when available, the source revision and whether the source
had uncommitted changes.
